title: feat(types): a form field of type grid declares the grid widget's field-level keys (objectui#11070 round 10)
body:
Refs #11070
Clause-②: yes (widening). `FormFieldSchema`, a published accept set, accepts eight more keys on a form field entry, each one a key the `grid` widget already reads and `grid.mdx` teaches. The tolerant face now also judges their values, so a wrong-typed value it used to strip is refused. Both halves are priced in the changeset.

Round 10 of objectui#11070, under claim `5930921428` (`domain:devx` seat 2, maintainer direct dispatch R5). It has three items:

- (i) the grid widget's field-level keys on the form-field face, the seat's answer A in `5928627070`;
- (ii) one real run of objectui's strict authoring face over objectstack `examples/app-crm`, for objectstack-ai/objectstack#20960's acceptance item 3 (measure only, nothing changed for it);
- (iii) `grid.mdx`'s "Integration with Advanced Grid" section (finding 2 of `5929940616`).

## (i) The form-field face mirror

### Measured first, at base `0a3e5409`

- `GridFieldMetadata` declares, beyond `BaseFieldMetadata`, `columns` (round 7) and exactly the eight keys in the table below.
- Neither form-field face declared any of the eight. `FormField` resolved each one through its `[key: string]: any` index signature. `FormFieldSchema`, a plain `z.object`, stripped each one.
- The face is flat, not discriminated by `type`. `FormField` is one interface with `type?: string`, and `FormFieldSchema` is one `z.object(...).superRefine(...)`. Round 7 added `columns` to it the same way.
- No collision:
  - no `FormField` member has any of the eight names;
  - `@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0's `FieldSchema` declares none of them, so no spec change is involved;
  - in `@object-ui/fields`, `GridField` is the only reader. `MasterDetailForm` and `LineItemsPanel` write the same keys into the grid's config with the same meaning, and the `form` renderer reads none of them.
- Reach through the public door, by a scratch render probe (never committed) of the new fixture through `SchemaRenderer`, the real `form` renderer and `GridField`:
  - with the keys, the Add button reads "Add line item" and the footer shows the total 109.97;
  - the control, the same fixture without the keys, reads "Add line" and shows no total;
  - with `allow_add: false`, there is no Add button and no Duplicate action.

### Per key, both faces, before and after

| key | `GridFieldMetadata` | `FormField`: base → head | `FormFieldSchema`: base → head | strict face, `fields[]` grid entry: base → head | tolerant face: base → head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min_rows` | `number` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['min_rows']` | undeclared → `z.number().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.min_rows` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `"1"` refused |
| `max_rows` | `number` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['max_rows']` | undeclared → `z.number().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.max_rows` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `"20"` refused |
| `allow_add` | `boolean` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['allow_add']` | undeclared → `z.boolean().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.allow_add` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `"false"` refused |
| `allow_delete` | `boolean` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['allow_delete']` | undeclared → `z.boolean().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.allow_delete` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `"false"` refused |
| `allow_reorder` | `boolean` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['allow_reorder']` | undeclared → `z.boolean().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.allow_reorder` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `"false"` refused |
| `total_field` | `string` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['total_field']` | undeclared → `z.string().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.total_field` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `3` refused |
| `add_label` | `string` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['add_label']` | undeclared → `z.string().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.add_label` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `1` refused |
| `sort_field` | `string` | index signature (`any`) → `GridFieldMetadata['sort_field']` | undeclared → `z.string().optional()` | refused by name at `fields.0.sort_field` → accepted | value stripped → value kept; `0` refused |

The base column was read by a scratch probe on the built `@object-ui/types` dist at `0a3e5409`, with a lit control: the same entry without the keys parses on both faces. Each `.describe()` on the zod side says that only the `grid` widget reads the key.

### Pins

- `strict-face-read-keys-11070.test.ts`:
  - block 1 gains one `fields[]` grid-entry row per key, each with a misspelled sibling still refused by name, plus an all-eight row whose tolerant output keeps every value;
  - block 2 gains one wrong-type row per key, refused on both faces;
  - block 4 gains `assertionGridFieldKeysOnTheFormFieldFace`. Every member `GridFieldMetadata` declares beyond `BaseFieldMetadata` must be a DECLARED `FormField` member (not the index signature) with the same type, so a key added to the grid's type and left unmirrored fails to compile. A lit control shows the key set it ranges over is non-empty.
- `form-field-zod-coverage.test.ts`: the eight keys join `DECLARED_KEYS`.
- `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`: `FormFieldSchema` was already a registered pair. The eight keys are LOCAL on both sides, so no ledger total moves. Its `SPEC_DERIVED_PAIRS` note now says so.

### The refusal flip and the ablations

Predictions were written before each run. Every mutation was committed first and restored to HEAD, with blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. A1 and A2 went through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, blob changed). The subjects resolve from source, since the tests import `../zod` relatively, so no dist is on the path.

- **R0, the refusal flip:** `form.zod.ts` and `form.ts` were set to base `0a3e5409`, and this head's pins were run against them.
  - Predicted: 18 red in vitest (8 per-key rows, the all-eight row, 8 wrong-type rows, the coverage key set) and tsc red only in the pin file.
  - Measured: `Tests 18 failed | 68 passed (86)`, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` gave 10 errors, all in `assertionGridFieldKeysOnTheFormFieldFace` (completeness, the mapped equality, the 8 per-key rows). `zod-mirror-parity` compiled.
- **A1, zod ablation:** the `allow_add` member was deleted from `FormFieldSchema`.
  - Predicted: 4 red (the `allow_add` row, the all-eight row, the wrong-type `allow_add` row, the coverage key set) and the parity file red at tsc.
  - Measured: `Tests 4 failed | 119 passed (123)` over the pin, coverage and parity files. tsc gave 1 error, in `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` at `assertionUnmirroredMatchesLedger` (`"form.zod.ts#FormFieldSchema"` is not assignable to `never`).
- **A2, TS ablation:** the `allow_add` member was deleted from `FormField`.
  - Predicted: vitest green, the type-level pin red, and the parity file red on the fourth direction.
  - Measured: `Tests 123 passed (123)`. tsc gave 5 errors: the pin file's completeness, mapped-equality and per-key `allow_add` rows, and `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`'s `MirroredUndeclared` reconciliation, by pair and by key (`"allow_add"` is not assignable to `never`).

### Fixture and docs

- `examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/fields-grid/line-items-grid.json` writes all eight keys, with columns and seeded rows, so the corpus exercises the declared set. The catalog index is regenerated.
- The three catalog DOM-leak census pins count the new entry, as their own text asks of an added example: `grid` goes from 26 to 27 in all three, and in the layout pin `text` goes from 698 to 699 rendered and from 154 to 155 with no element.
- `grid.mdx` embeds the fixture and says that the keys are accepted on a form field entry of `type: 'grid'`, and that only the `grid` widget reads them.

## (ii) The app-crm strict-face run (measure only)

**The instrument, and why it is the real one.** The run uses `StrictAnyComponentSchema`, exported by `@object-ui/types/zod` (the built `packages/types/dist/zod/index.zod.js`), called with `.safeParse`. That is the call PR #11069's `validateAuthoredDocument` makes for `objectui validate` and `objectui check`.
- It is the shipped, derived face (objectui#8345), not a replica.
- `scripts/measure-strict-authoring-face.mjs` is not the real face. Its own header says it keeps its own twin walker, PR #11069's M1 measured that walker behind the shipped face on registered inputs, and it walks only objectui's own corpora.
- On `main` the CLI still validates through the tolerant face (PR #11069 is parked), and neither the CLI nor that script reads TypeScript modules. So nothing in this repository walks an objectstack app.
- The walk itself is a scratch driver, never committed. It imports app-crm's UI modules with `tsx`, resolving `@objectstack/spec` to the installed 17.5.0, the version objectstack `main` declares. It hands each document to the face the way objectui's console hands it to a renderer.

**Command and shas.**
- objectui `0a3e5409`, the base, which is `main`. The types dist was built with `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`. The run was repeated on head `be58a328` with byte-identical output.
- objectstack `f0cc16e8d`, `origin/main`. `399e3aa97b` is its ancestor (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0), and `git diff 399e3aa97b f0cc16e8d -- examples/app-crm` is empty.
- app-crm was extracted with `git archive f0cc16e8d examples/app-crm`, and the run was `pnpm exec tsx appcrm-strict-run.mts OBJECTUI_WORKTREE APP_CRM_EXTRACT BEFORE_DASHBOARD`.

| app-crm document | projection | tolerant | strict | refusals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dashboards/pipeline.dashboard.ts` · `PipelineDashboard` | `{ type: 'dashboard', ...doc }`: `DashboardView` hands the stored document to `DashboardRenderer`, and objectui's node face for it is the `dashboard` arm | PASS | **PASS** | none |
| `pages/welcome.page.ts` · `CrmWelcomePage` | `{ ...page, type: 'page', pageType: page.type }`: the `page` arm, with the kind on `pageType` | PASS | PASS | none |
| the same page, as `PageView` writes it | `{ ...page, type: page.type, pageType: page.type }`, so `type: 'home'` | FAIL | FAIL | `invalid_union` at `type` (no matching discriminator) on both faces. This is the page-kind / node-type collision documented in `layout.zod.ts`'s `PAGE_SPEC_EXCLUDED` note (objectui#9642), not an unknown key. |
| `apps/crm.app.ts` · `CrmApp` | `{ type: 'app', ...doc }` | PASS | PASS | none |
| **lit control:** `pipeline.dashboard.ts` at `399e3aa97b^` (`39ab2940e`) | `{ type: 'dashboard', ...doc }` | PASS | FAIL | `unrecognized_keys` `[format, currency]` at `widgets.0.options`, `widgets.1.options` and `widgets.2.options` (plus the non-viable `metric-card` slot arm's own issues) |

- The dashboard pair objectstack#20960 removed (`options.format` / `options.currency`) does not appear at `f0cc16e8d`, and the control shows that the face refuses exactly that pair before the removal.
- Nothing in app-crm's UI documents is refused by an unknown key.
- Not judged: objects, views, actions, flows, datasets, datasources, hooks, security, translations and seed data. These are server metadata, not objectui node documents, and the console builds its list and form nodes from views in code, so there is no single stored-document projection to judge.

## (iii) `grid.mdx` — "Integration with Advanced Grid"

The section offered seven features as `@object-ui/plugin-grid`'s. The basic grid field has five of them too: inline editing, add and remove, row drag-reorder, computed columns, and a one-column footer total. `object-grid` has no computed columns, and it reorders columns, not rows. It is now a table of what each widget reads, feature by feature, each cell checked against the reader:

- **inline editing:** `GridField`'s cell controls versus `object-grid`'s `editable`, ANDed with the principal's write verdict;
- **add and remove:** `allow_add` / `allow_delete` versus `operations.create` and `operations.delete` with the host's `onDelete`;
- **sorting and filtering:** none in the grid field, versus header sort, `sortable: false`, `filter` / `sort` and `searchableFields`;
- **drag reorder:** rows through `allow_reorder` and `sort_field`, versus columns only through `reorderableColumns`;
- **export:** none, versus `exportOptions`;
- **computed columns:** `computed` with `expr` in the grid field, versus none in `object-grid` (a formula field is shown as served);
- **totals:** `total_field`, versus `columns[].summary` and group `aggregations`.

- **Docs and changeset gates, green:** `check:doc-snippets` (769 of 769 blocks, 0 failed), `check:doc-fences`, `docs:check-links`, `check:doc-example-ids`, `check:doc-types`, `check:doc-examples`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check-type-check-coverage`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), the catalog `regenerate:check`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-presence`, `changeset:check`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` (NOT GOVERNED).

  - The population is the config's `**/*.{ts,tsx}` blocks. The JSON, MDX and MD files match none.

`main` did not move after the base (`0a3e5409`), so there was nothing to merge before opening.

**Changeset:** `@object-ui/types` **minor**. A published accept set widens by eight keys, and the tolerant face narrows on their values. The breaking half is stated in the changeset and priced minor under the fixed group's policy. Nothing else ships: the `@object-ui/fields` edit is a test docblock, and the catalog is private.

## Acceptance notes

- **The flat-face boundary.** The eight keys are accepted on every `fields[]` entry, and only the `grid` widget reads them, exactly as with `columns`. Moving them to a `type`-discriminated arm would be a ruling, not this round's work.
- **Value rules.** `min_rows` and `max_rows` are typed `number` on both faces, as `GridFieldMetadata` types them. No integer or range rule was added: that would tighten `GridFieldMetadata` too, which is a contract decision.
- **Two edits beyond the named surface:**
  - the docblock of `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.declaredSpelling.test.tsx` said "the three `fields-grid` catalog examples", which the new fixture made stale; it now says "every";
  - the three DOM-leak census pins, as above.
- **The as-served page projection.** `type: 'home'` has no arm on either face, which is the collision objectui#9642 documents. It is an observation and is not filed.
